from typing import Annotated

from fastapi import APIRouter, Cookie, Depends, Response, status

from app.api.deps import AppSettings, DbSession, require_csrf_header
from app.core.config import Settings
from app.schemas.auth import LoginRequest, RegisterRequest, TokenResponse
from app.schemas.user import UserRead
from app.services import auth_service
from app.services.auth_service import AuthResult

REFRESH_COOKIE = "fv_refresh"
# The cookie is only ever sent to the auth endpoints, never to data endpoints.
REFRESH_COOKIE_PATH = "/api/v1/auth"

router = APIRouter(prefix="/auth", tags=["auth"])


def _set_refresh_cookie(response: Response, token: str, max_age: int, settings: Settings) -> None:
    response.set_cookie(
        REFRESH_COOKIE,
        token,
        max_age=max_age,
        httponly=True,
        secure=settings.cookie_secure,
        samesite=settings.cookie_samesite,
        path=REFRESH_COOKIE_PATH,
    )


def _clear_refresh_cookie(response: Response, settings: Settings) -> None:
    response.delete_cookie(
        REFRESH_COOKIE,
        path=REFRESH_COOKIE_PATH,
        httponly=True,
        secure=settings.cookie_secure,
        samesite=settings.cookie_samesite,
    )


def _respond(result: AuthResult, response: Response, settings: Settings) -> TokenResponse:
    _set_refresh_cookie(response, result.refresh_token, result.refresh_max_age, settings)
    return TokenResponse(
        access_token=result.access_token,
        expires_in=result.expires_in,
        user=UserRead.model_validate(result.user),
    )


@router.post("/register", response_model=TokenResponse, status_code=status.HTTP_201_CREATED)
def register(
    body: RegisterRequest, response: Response, db: DbSession, settings: AppSettings
) -> TokenResponse:
    return _respond(auth_service.register(db, settings, body), response, settings)


@router.post("/login", response_model=TokenResponse)
def login(
    body: LoginRequest, response: Response, db: DbSession, settings: AppSettings
) -> TokenResponse:
    return _respond(auth_service.login(db, settings, body), response, settings)


@router.post("/refresh", response_model=TokenResponse, dependencies=[Depends(require_csrf_header)])
def refresh(
    response: Response,
    db: DbSession,
    settings: AppSettings,
    refresh_token: Annotated[str | None, Cookie(alias=REFRESH_COOKIE)] = None,
) -> TokenResponse:
    try:
        result = auth_service.refresh(db, settings, refresh_token)
    except Exception:
        # A failed refresh must not leave a stale cookie behind in the browser.
        _clear_refresh_cookie(response, settings)
        raise
    return _respond(result, response, settings)


@router.post(
    "/logout", status_code=status.HTTP_204_NO_CONTENT, dependencies=[Depends(require_csrf_header)]
)
def logout(
    response: Response,
    db: DbSession,
    settings: AppSettings,
    refresh_token: Annotated[str | None, Cookie(alias=REFRESH_COOKIE)] = None,
) -> None:
    auth_service.logout(db, refresh_token)
    _clear_refresh_cookie(response, settings)

import uuid
from typing import Annotated
from urllib.parse import quote

from fastapi import APIRouter, Depends, File, Query, UploadFile, status
from fastapi.responses import StreamingResponse

from app.api.deps import AppSettings, CurrentUser, DbSession, Storage, require_csrf_header
from app.repositories import media as media_repo
from app.schemas.common import Page
from app.schemas.media import MediaRead
from app.services import media_service

router = APIRouter(prefix="/media", tags=["media"])


@router.post(
    "",
    response_model=MediaRead,
    status_code=status.HTTP_201_CREATED,
    dependencies=[Depends(require_csrf_header)],
)
def upload_media(
    file: Annotated[UploadFile, File(description="JPEG, PNG or WebP image")],
    user: CurrentUser,
    db: DbSession,
    storage: Storage,
    settings: AppSettings,
) -> MediaRead:
    return MediaRead.model_validate(media_service.upload(db, storage, settings, user, file))


@router.get("", response_model=Page[MediaRead])
def list_media(
    user: CurrentUser,
    db: DbSession,
    page: Annotated[int, Query(ge=1, le=100_000)] = 1,
    page_size: Annotated[int, Query(ge=1, le=50)] = 12,
) -> Page[MediaRead]:
    rows, total = media_repo.list_page(db, user.id, limit=page_size, offset=(page - 1) * page_size)
    return Page.build([MediaRead.model_validate(r) for r in rows], total, page, page_size)


@router.get("/{media_id}", response_model=MediaRead)
def get_media(media_id: uuid.UUID, user: CurrentUser, db: DbSession) -> MediaRead:
    return MediaRead.model_validate(media_service.get_owned_or_404(db, user, media_id))


@router.get("/{media_id}/content")
def get_media_content(
    media_id: uuid.UUID,
    user: CurrentUser,
    db: DbSession,
    storage: Storage,
    download: bool = False,
) -> StreamingResponse:
    asset, stream = media_service.open_content(db, storage, user, media_id)
    disposition = "inline"
    if download:
        disposition = f"attachment; filename*=UTF-8''{quote(asset.display_name, safe='')}"
    return StreamingResponse(
        stream,
        media_type=asset.content_type,  # from our own detection, never the client's claim
        headers={
            "Content-Length": str(asset.size_bytes),
            "Content-Disposition": disposition,
            # Defence in depth: even if rendered as a document, nothing may execute or load.
            "Content-Security-Policy": "default-src 'none'; sandbox",
            "Cache-Control": "private, no-store",
        },
    )


@router.delete(
    "/{media_id}",
    status_code=status.HTTP_204_NO_CONTENT,
    dependencies=[Depends(require_csrf_header)],
)
def delete_media(media_id: uuid.UUID, user: CurrentUser, db: DbSession, storage: Storage) -> None:
    media_service.delete(db, storage, user, media_id)

FILE: backend/app/api/v1/nutrition.py

from typing import Annotated

from fastapi import APIRouter, Path, Query

from app.api.deps import AppSettings, CurrentUser, Nutrition
from app.core.errors import AppError
from app.core.limits import limiter
from app.nutrition.service import clean_query
from app.schemas.food import BarcodeResponse, NutritionSearchResponse
from app.services import food_service

router = APIRouter(prefix="/nutrition", tags=["nutrition"])


@router.get("/search", response_model=NutritionSearchResponse)
def search(
    user: CurrentUser,
    settings: AppSettings,
    nutrition: Nutrition,
    q: Annotated[str, Query(min_length=2, max_length=80)],
    limit: Annotated[int, Query(ge=1, le=15)] = 8,
) -> NutritionSearchResponse:
    """Find trusted nutrition records for a food name. Failing sources are reported, not hidden."""
    cleaned = clean_query(q)
    if len(cleaned) < 2:
        raise AppError("Enter at least two letters.", code="invalid_query", status_code=422)
    limiter("food search", settings.nutrition_search_rate_limit_per_minute).check(str(user.id))
    outcome = nutrition.search(cleaned, limit)
    return NutritionSearchResponse(
        query=cleaned,
        results=[food_service.candidate_out(settings, user, c) for c in outcome.results],
        sources=outcome.sources,
    )


@router.get("/barcode/{barcode}", response_model=BarcodeResponse)
def barcode(
    barcode: Annotated[str, Path(pattern=r"^\d{8,14}$")],
    user: CurrentUser,
    settings: AppSettings,
    nutrition: Nutrition,
) -> BarcodeResponse:
    limiter("food search", settings.nutrition_search_rate_limit_per_minute).check(str(user.id))
    found, sources = nutrition.barcode(barcode)
    return BarcodeResponse(
        barcode=barcode,
        result=food_service.candidate_out(settings, user, found) if found else None,
        sources=sources,
    )

FILE: backend/app/api/v1/system.py
================================================================================

from functools import lru_cache
from typing import Annotated

from alembic.config import Config
from alembic.script import ScriptDirectory
from fastapi import APIRouter, Depends
from fastapi.responses import JSONResponse
from sqlalchemy import text
from sqlalchemy.exc import SQLAlchemyError

from app.ai.ollama import OllamaClient
from app.api.deps import CurrentUser, DbSession, get_ollama_client
from app.core.config import BACKEND_DIR
from app.schemas.meta import PreferenceOptions
from app.schemas.system import AIStatus, HealthResponse

router = APIRouter(tags=["system"])


@lru_cache
def _migration_head() -> str | None:
    cfg = Config(str(BACKEND_DIR / "alembic.ini"))
    cfg.set_main_option("script_location", str(BACKEND_DIR / "alembic"))
    return ScriptDirectory.from_config(cfg).get_current_head()


@router.get("/health", response_model=HealthResponse)
def health() -> HealthResponse:
    """Liveness: the process is up. Does not touch the database."""
    return HealthResponse(status="ok")


@router.get("/ready", response_model=HealthResponse, responses={503: {"model": HealthResponse}})
def ready(db: DbSession) -> HealthResponse | JSONResponse:
    """Readiness: the database is reachable and migrations are at the latest revision."""
    checks: dict[str, str] = {}
    try:
        db.execute(text("SELECT 1"))
        checks["database"] = "ok"
    except SQLAlchemyError:
        checks["database"] = "unreachable"
        return JSONResponse(
            HealthResponse(status="unavailable", checks=checks).model_dump(), status_code=503
        )
    try:
        current = db.execute(text("SELECT version_num FROM alembic_version")).scalar()
    except SQLAlchemyError:
        db.rollback()
        current = None
    checks["migrations"] = "ok" if current == _migration_head() else "not_up_to_date"
    if checks["migrations"] != "ok":
        return JSONResponse(
            HealthResponse(status="unavailable", checks=checks).model_dump(), status_code=503
        )
    return HealthResponse(status="ok", checks=checks)


@router.get("/meta/preference-options", response_model=PreferenceOptions)
def preference_options() -> PreferenceOptions:
    return PreferenceOptions.current()


@router.get("/ai/status", response_model=AIStatus)
def ai_status(
    _user: CurrentUser, client: Annotated[OllamaClient, Depends(get_ollama_client)]
) -> AIStatus:
    """Read-only: what AI is configured and reachable. Never downloads or runs a model."""
    return client.status()

"""Application configuration, loaded from environment variables (and an optional .env file).

Nothing here has a secret default: the app refuses to start without DATABASE_URL and
JWT_SECRET_KEY. AI settings are opt-in and never imply a paid provider.
"""

from functools import lru_cache
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Literal

from pydantic import Field, SecretStr, field_validator, model_validator
from pydantic_settings import BaseSettings, SettingsConfigDict

BACKEND_DIR = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]


class Settings(BaseSettings):
    model_config = SettingsConfigDict(
        env_file=BACKEND_DIR / ".env",
        env_file_encoding="utf-8",
        extra="ignore",
    )

    # --- General ---
    app_env: Literal["development", "test", "production"] = "development"
    log_level: Literal["DEBUG", "INFO", "WARNING", "ERROR"] = "INFO"
    enable_api_docs: bool = True

    # --- Database ---
    database_url: str

    # --- Auth / sessions (see docs/adr/0001-auth-session-strategy.md) ---
    jwt_secret_key: str = Field(min_length=32)
    access_token_expire_minutes: int = Field(default=15, ge=1, le=60)
    refresh_token_expire_days: int = Field(default=14, ge=1, le=90)
    cookie_secure: bool = True
    cookie_samesite: Literal["strict", "lax", "none"] = "strict"

    # --- CORS (comma-separated list of exact origins) ---
    cors_allowed_origins: str = "http://localhost:5173"

    # --- AI (all optional; nothing is downloaded or called unless enabled) ---
    ollama_enabled: bool = False
    ollama_base_url: str = "http://localhost:11434"
    ollama_text_model: str = ""
    ollama_vision_model: str = ""
    ollama_timeout_seconds: float = Field(default=120.0, gt=0, le=1800)
    allow_external_ai_providers: bool = False

    # --- Vision (food recognition). See docs/adr/0003-food-recognition-and-nutrition.md ---
    vision_provider: Literal["ollama", "openai_compatible"] = "ollama"
    vision_api_base_url: str = ""
    vision_api_key: SecretStr | None = None
    vision_api_model: str = ""
    vision_timeout_seconds: float = Field(default=120.0, gt=0, le=1800)

    # --- Text (cooking assistant, Phase 6). Same policy: opt-in, explicit, no fallback. ---
    text_provider: Literal["ollama", "openai_compatible"] = "ollama"
    text_api_base_url: str = ""
    text_api_key: SecretStr | None = None
    text_api_model: str = ""
    text_timeout_seconds: float = Field(default=180.0, gt=0, le=3600)

    # --- Cooking assistant ---
    cooking_rate_limit_per_minute: int = Field(default=10, ge=1, le=600)
    cooking_context_messages: int = Field(default=12, ge=2, le=40)
    cooking_context_chars: int = Field(default=12_000, ge=1_000, le=100_000)

    # --- Nutrition data sources (all optional; each is only used when configured) ---
    usda_fdc_api_key: SecretStr | None = None
    usda_fdc_base_url: str = "https://api.nal.usda.gov/fdc/v1"
    open_food_facts_enabled: bool = False
    open_food_facts_base_url: str = "https://world.openfoodfacts.org"
    open_food_facts_user_agent: str = "FoodVerseAI/0.1 (self-hosted)"
    nutrition_timeout_seconds: float = Field(default=10.0, gt=0, le=60)
    signed_ref_ttl_minutes: int = Field(default=720, ge=5, le=10_080)

    # --- Per-user rate limits (in-process; protects model CPU and third-party API quotas) ---
    scan_rate_limit_per_minute: int = Field(default=6, ge=1, le=600)
    nutrition_search_rate_limit_per_minute: int = Field(default=30, ge=1, le=600)

    # --- Media (see docs/adr/0002-media-storage.md) ---
    media_root: Path = Path.home() / ".foodverse" / "media"
    max_upload_bytes: int = Field(default=8 * 1024 * 1024, ge=1024, le=64 * 1024 * 1024)
    max_image_pixels: int = Field(default=40_000_000, ge=10_000, le=200_000_000)
    user_media_quota_bytes: int = Field(default=500 * 1024 * 1024, ge=1024)

    @field_validator("media_root")
    @classmethod
    def _absolute_media_root(cls, value: Path) -> Path:
        return value.expanduser().resolve()

    @field_validator("database_url")
    @classmethod
    def _normalise_database_url(cls, value: str) -> str:
        if value.startswith("postgresql://"):
            value = value.replace("postgresql://", "postgresql+psycopg://", 1)
        if not value.startswith("postgresql+psycopg://"):
            raise ValueError("DATABASE_URL must be a PostgreSQL URL (postgresql+psycopg://...)")
        return value

    @field_validator("cors_allowed_origins")
    @classmethod
    def _validate_cors(cls, value: str) -> str:
        for origin in (o.strip() for o in value.split(",") if o.strip()):
            if origin == "*":
                raise ValueError("CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS must not contain '*' (credentials are used)")
            if not origin.startswith(("http://", "https://")):
                raise ValueError(f"Invalid CORS origin: {origin!r}")
        return value

    @field_validator("ollama_base_url")
    @classmethod
    def _validate_ollama_url(cls, value: str) -> str:
        if not value.startswith(("http://", "https://")):
            raise ValueError("OLLAMA_BASE_URL must start with http:// or https://")
        return value.rstrip("/")

    @field_validator(
        "vision_api_base_url",
        "text_api_base_url",
        "usda_fdc_base_url",
        "open_food_facts_base_url",
    )
    @classmethod
    def _validate_http_url(cls, value: str) -> str:
        """Single validator for every optional URL field. Empty is allowed (means unset)."""
        if value and not value.startswith(("http://", "https://")):
            raise ValueError("URL settings must start with http:// or https://")
        return value.rstrip("/")

    @model_validator(mode="after")
    def _vision_guards(self) -> "Settings":
        if self.vision_provider == "openai_compatible":
            if not self.allow_external_ai_providers:
                raise ValueError(
                    "VISION_PROVIDER=openai_compatible requires ALLOW_EXTERNAL_AI_PROVIDERS=true "
                    "(the photo is sent to that server; this must be an explicit choice)"
                )
            if not self.vision_api_base_url or not self.vision_api_model:
                raise ValueError(
                    "VISION_API_BASE_URL and VISION_API_MODEL are required for openai_compatible"
                )
        return self

    @model_validator(mode="after")
    def _text_guards(self) -> "Settings":
        if self.text_provider == "openai_compatible":
            if not self.allow_external_ai_providers:
                raise ValueError(
                    "TEXT_PROVIDER=openai_compatible requires ALLOW_EXTERNAL_AI_PROVIDERS=true "
                    "(prompts are sent to that server; this must be an explicit choice)"
                )
            if not self.text_api_base_url or not self.text_api_model:
                raise ValueError(
                    "TEXT_API_BASE_URL and TEXT_API_MODEL are required for openai_compatible"
                )
        return self

    @model_validator(mode="after")
    def _production_guards(self) -> "Settings":
        if self.cookie_samesite == "none" and not self.cookie_secure:
            raise ValueError("COOKIE_SAMESITE=none requires COOKIE_SECURE=true")
        if self.app_env == "production":
            if self.jwt_secret_key.lower().startswith("replace"):
                raise ValueError("JWT_SECRET_KEY is still the placeholder value")
            if not self.cookie_secure:
                raise ValueError("COOKIE_SECURE must be true in production")
            if not self.cors_origins:
                raise ValueError("CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS must be set in production")
        return self

    @property
    def cors_origins(self) -> list[str]:
        return [o.strip() for o in self.cors_allowed_origins.split(",") if o.strip()]


@lru_cache
def get_settings() -> Settings:
    return Settings()

================================================================================
FILE: backend/app/core/errors.py

"""Consistent error responses.

Every error has the shape:
    {"error": {"code": str, "message": str, "details": [...] | null, "request_id": str | null}}

Validation errors deliberately omit the submitted input so passwords are never echoed back.
"""

import logging
from typing import Any

from fastapi import FastAPI, Request
from fastapi.exceptions import RequestValidationError
from fastapi.responses import JSONResponse
from starlette.exceptions import HTTPException as StarletteHTTPException

logger = logging.getLogger("app.errors")


class AppError(Exception):
    status_code = 400
    code = "bad_request"

    def __init__(
        self,
        message: str,
        *,
        code: str | None = None,
        status_code: int | None = None,
        headers: dict[str, str] | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        super().__init__(message)
        self.message = message
        if code is not None:
            self.code = code
        if status_code is not None:
            self.status_code = status_code
        self.headers = headers


class NotAuthenticatedError(AppError):
    status_code = 401
    code = "not_authenticated"

    def __init__(self, message: str = "Authentication required.", *, code: str | None = None):
        super().__init__(message, code=code, headers={"WWW-Authenticate": "Bearer"})


class InvalidCredentialsError(AppError):
    status_code = 401
    code = "invalid_credentials"


class ConflictError(AppError):
    status_code = 409
    code = "conflict"


class ForbiddenError(AppError):
    status_code = 403
    code = "forbidden"


class NotFoundError(AppError):
    status_code = 404
    code = "not_found"


class PayloadTooLargeError(AppError):
    status_code = 413
    code = "file_too_large"


class UnsupportedMediaTypeError(AppError):
    status_code = 415
    code = "unsupported_media_type"


class RateLimitedError(AppError):
    status_code = 429
    code = "rate_limited"

    def __init__(self, message: str, *, retry_after: int) -> None:
        super().__init__(message, headers={"Retry-After": str(max(1, retry_after))})


def _body(
    code: str, message: str, request: Request, details: list[dict[str, Any]] | None = None
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    return {
        "error": {
            "code": code,
            "message": message,
            "details": details,
            "request_id": getattr(request.state, "request_id", None),
        }
    }


def register_exception_handlers(app: FastAPI) -> None:
    @app.exception_handler(AppError)
    async def _app_error(request: Request, exc: AppError) -> JSONResponse:
        return JSONResponse(
            _body(exc.code, exc.message, request), status_code=exc.status_code, headers=exc.headers
        )

    @app.exception_handler(RequestValidationError)
    async def _validation_error(request: Request, exc: RequestValidationError) -> JSONResponse:
        details = [
            {
                "field": ".".join(str(part) for part in err["loc"] if part != "body"),
                "message": err["msg"],
            }
            for err in exc.errors()
        ]
        return JSONResponse(
            _body("validation_error", "Request validation failed.", request, details),
            status_code=422,
        )

    @app.exception_handler(StarletteHTTPException)
    async def _http_error(request: Request, exc: StarletteHTTPException) -> JSONResponse:
        code = {404: "not_found", 405: "method_not_allowed"}.get(exc.status_code, "http_error")
        message = exc.detail if isinstance(exc.detail, str) else "Request failed."
        return JSONResponse(
            _body(code, message, request),
            status_code=exc.status_code,
            headers=getattr(exc, "headers", None),
        )

    @app.exception_handler(Exception)
    async def _unhandled(request: Request, exc: Exception) -> JSONResponse:
        # Log type and request id only; the exception text may contain user data.
        logger.error(
            "unhandled_exception type=%s request_id=%s",
            type(exc).__name__,
            getattr(request.state, "request_id", None),
            exc_info=exc,
        )
        return JSONResponse(
            _body("internal_error", "An unexpected error occurred.", request), status_code=500
        )

"""Named per-user rate limiters shared across requests (in-process; see ratelimit.py)."""

from app.core.ratelimit import SlidingWindowLimiter

_limiters: dict[str, SlidingWindowLimiter] = {}


def limiter(name: str, limit: int) -> SlidingWindowLimiter:
    existing = _limiters.get(name)
    if existing is None or existing.limit != limit:
        existing = _limiters[name] = SlidingWindowLimiter(name, limit)
    return existing


def reset_limiters() -> None:
    for item in _limiters.values():
        item.reset()

================================================================================
FILE: backend/app/core/logging.py

"""Logging setup with a per-request id. Request/response bodies are never logged."""

import logging
from contextvars import ContextVar

request_id_ctx: ContextVar[str | None] = ContextVar("request_id", default=None)


class RequestIdFilter(logging.Filter):
    def filter(self, record: logging.LogRecord) -> bool:
        record.request_id = request_id_ctx.get() or "-"
        return True


def configure_logging(level: str) -> None:
    handler = logging.StreamHandler()
    handler.addFilter(RequestIdFilter())
    handler.setFormatter(
        logging.Formatter("%(asctime)s %(levelname)s [%(request_id)s] %(name)s: %(message)s")
    )
    root = logging.getLogger()
    root.handlers = [handler]
    root.setLevel(level)
    # SQL statements can contain user data; keep the engine quiet regardless of root level.
    logging.getLogger("sqlalchemy.engine").setLevel(logging.WARNING)
    logging.getLogger("uvicorn.access").disabled = True  # replaced by our own access log
    # httpx logs every request URL at INFO. Some upstream APIs (USDA FoodData Central) take the
    # API key as a query parameter, so those lines would write secrets to the log.
    for noisy in ("httpx", "httpcore"):
        logging.getLogger(noisy).setLevel(logging.WARNING)

================================================================================
FILE: backend/app/core/middleware.py
================================================================================

"""Pure-ASGI middleware: request id, access log, and baseline security headers.

Written as raw ASGI (not BaseHTTPMiddleware) so the request id is available to exception
handlers and so response headers are applied to every response, including errors.
Query strings and bodies are never logged.
"""

import json
import logging
import time
import uuid

from starlette.datastructures import MutableHeaders
from starlette.types import ASGIApp, Message, Receive, Scope, Send

from app.core.errors import PayloadTooLargeError
from app.core.logging import request_id_ctx

logger = logging.getLogger("app.access")

_SECURITY_HEADERS = {
    "X-Content-Type-Options": "nosniff",
    "X-Frame-Options": "DENY",
    "Referrer-Policy": "no-referrer",
    "Cache-Control": "no-store",
}


class RequestContextMiddleware:
    def __init__(self, app: ASGIApp) -> None:
        self.app = app

    async def __call__(self, scope: Scope, receive: Receive, send: Send) -> None:
        if scope["type"] != "http":
            await self.app(scope, receive, send)
            return

        request_id = uuid.uuid4().hex
        scope.setdefault("state", {})["request_id"] = request_id
        token = request_id_ctx.set(request_id)
        started = time.perf_counter()
        status_code = 500

        async def send_wrapper(message: Message) -> None:
            nonlocal status_code
            if message["type"] == "http.response.start":
                status_code = message["status"]
                headers = MutableHeaders(scope=message)
                headers["X-Request-ID"] = request_id
                for name, value in _SECURITY_HEADERS.items():
                    headers.setdefault(name, value)
            await send(message)

        try:
            await self.app(scope, receive, send_wrapper)
        finally:
            logger.info(
                "%s %s -> %s (%.1f ms)",
                scope["method"],
                scope["path"],
                status_code,
                (time.perf_counter() - started) * 1000,
            )
            request_id_ctx.reset(token)


class _BodyTooLarge(Exception):
    """Raised from `receive` to abort body parsing once the limit is exceeded."""


class BodySizeLimitMiddleware:
    """Reject oversized request bodies before they are buffered.

    Checks Content-Length up front (no body is read at all) and also counts bytes as they
    stream in, so a client that lies about, or omits, Content-Length cannot push an unbounded
    body through. The 413 is written here rather than raised as an app error because FastAPI
    rewrites exceptions raised during body parsing into a generic 400.
    """

    def __init__(self, app: ASGIApp, *, max_bytes: int, path_prefix: str) -> None:
        self.app = app
        self.max_bytes = max_bytes
        self.path_prefix = path_prefix

    async def __call__(self, scope: Scope, receive: Receive, send: Send) -> None:
        if scope["type"] != "http" or not scope["path"].startswith(self.path_prefix):
            await self.app(scope, receive, send)
            return

        declared = dict(scope["headers"]).get(b"content-length")
        if declared is not None and declared.isdigit() and int(declared) > self.max_bytes:
            await self._reject(scope, send)
            return

        received = 0
        tripped = False

        async def limited_receive() -> Message:
            nonlocal received, tripped
            message = await receive()
            if message["type"] == "http.request":
                received += len(message.get("body", b""))
                if received > self.max_bytes:
                    tripped = True
                    raise _BodyTooLarge
            return message

        async def guarded_send(message: Message) -> None:
            if tripped:  # discard whatever the app produced; we answer 413 ourselves
                return
            await send(message)

        try:
            await self.app(scope, limited_receive, guarded_send)
        except _BodyTooLarge:
            pass
        if tripped:
            await self._reject(scope, send)

    async def _reject(self, scope: Scope, send: Send) -> None:
        error = PayloadTooLargeError("Request body is too large.")
        body = json.dumps(
            {
                "error": {
                    "code": error.code,
                    "message": error.message,
                    "details": None,
                    "request_id": scope.get("state", {}).get("request_id"),
                }
            }
        ).encode()
        await send(
            {
                "type": "http.response.start",
                "status": error.status_code,
                "headers": [
                    (b"content-type", b"application/json"),
                    (b"content-length", str(len(body)).encode()),
                    (b"connection", b"close"),
                ],
            }
        )
        await send({"type": "http.response.body", "body": body})

FILE: backend/app/core/ratelimit.py
================================================================================

"""Small in-process sliding-window rate limiter, keyed per user.

It protects model CPU time and third-party API quotas (e.g. USDA's per-key hourly limit). It is
per-process: with several workers each has its own window. Use a shared store (Redis) if the app
is ever scaled out; the interface would stay the same.
"""

import threading
import time
from collections import defaultdict, deque

from app.core.errors import RateLimitedError


class SlidingWindowLimiter:
    def __init__(self, name: str, limit: int, window_seconds: float = 60.0) -> None:
        self.name = name
        self.limit = limit
        self.window = window_seconds
        self._hits: dict[str, deque[float]] = defaultdict(deque)
        self._lock = threading.Lock()

    def check(self, key: str) -> None:
        now = time.monotonic()
        with self._lock:
            hits = self._hits[key]
            while hits and now - hits[0] >= self.window:
                hits.popleft()
            if len(hits) >= self.limit:
                retry = int(self.window - (now - hits[0])) + 1
                raise RateLimitedError(
                    f"Too many {self.name} requests. Please wait {retry} seconds and try again.",
                    retry_after=retry,
                )
            hits.append(now)

    def reset(self) -> None:
        with self._lock:
            self._hits.clear()

"""Password hashing and token primitives. No database access here."""

import hashlib
import secrets
from datetime import UTC, datetime, timedelta
from typing import Any

import jwt
from argon2 import PasswordHasher
from argon2.exceptions import InvalidHashError, VerificationError

from app.core.config import Settings

_hasher = PasswordHasher()  # argon2id with the library's current recommended parameters
JWT_ALGORITHM = "HS256"
ACCESS_TOKEN_TYPE = "access"  # noqa: S105  (a claim name, not a secret)

# Verified against when the account does not exist, so login timing does not reveal
# whether an email is registered.
_DUMMY_HASH = _hasher.hash("not-a-real-password")


def hash_password(password: str) -> str:
    return _hasher.hash(password)


def verify_password(password_hash: str, password: str) -> bool:
    try:
        return _hasher.verify(password_hash, password)
    except (VerificationError, InvalidHashError):
        return False


def verify_dummy_password(password: str) -> None:
    verify_password(_DUMMY_HASH, password)


def password_needs_rehash(password_hash: str) -> bool:
    return _hasher.check_needs_rehash(password_hash)


def create_access_token(user_id: str, settings: Settings) -> tuple[str, int]:
    """Return (token, expires_in_seconds)."""
    now = datetime.now(UTC)
    expires_in = settings.access_token_expire_minutes * 60
    payload: dict[str, Any] = {
        "sub": user_id,
        "type": ACCESS_TOKEN_TYPE,
        "iat": now,
        "exp": now + timedelta(seconds=expires_in),
    }
    return jwt.encode(payload, settings.jwt_secret_key, algorithm=JWT_ALGORITHM), expires_in


def decode_access_token(token: str, settings: Settings) -> str | None:
    """Return the user id for a valid access token, otherwise None."""
    try:
        payload = jwt.decode(
            token,
            settings.jwt_secret_key,
            algorithms=[JWT_ALGORITHM],
            options={"require": ["exp", "iat", "sub"]},
        )
    except jwt.PyJWTError:
        return None
    if payload.get("type") != ACCESS_TOKEN_TYPE or not isinstance(payload.get("sub"), str):
        return None
    return str(payload["sub"])


def generate_refresh_token() -> str:
    return secrets.token_urlsafe(48)


def hash_refresh_token(token: str) -> str:
    # High-entropy random token, so a fast hash is appropriate (no password-style stretching).
    return hashlib.sha256(token.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()

================================================================================
FILE: backend/app/core/signed_refs.py
================================================================================

"""Tamper-proof references the client carries between steps.

The server never trusts model output or nutrient values echoed back by the browser. Instead, when
it produces a scan result or a nutrition candidate it signs the payload (HMAC-SHA256, bound to the
user and an expiry). The client sends the opaque token back, and the server verifies it and uses
the *embedded* data. This is how "the model identifies, the user confirms, trusted data supplies
the numbers" stays true even though the browser relays everything.

Tokens are signed, not encrypted: do not put secrets in them.
"""

import base64
import hashlib
import hmac
import json
import time
import uuid
from typing import Any

from app.core.config import Settings
from app.core.errors import AppError

_DOMAIN = b"foodverse.signed-ref.v1:"


class InvalidRefError(AppError):
    status_code = 422

    def __init__(self, message: str = "This reference is invalid or has expired.") -> None:
        super().__init__(message, code="invalid_reference")


def _key(settings: Settings, kind: str) -> bytes:
    return hashlib.sha256(
        _DOMAIN + kind.encode() + b":" + settings.jwt_secret_key.encode()
    ).digest()


def _b64(data: bytes) -> str:
    return base64.urlsafe_b64encode(data).rstrip(b"=").decode()


def _unb64(text: str) -> bytes:
    return base64.urlsafe_b64decode(text + "=" * (-len(text) % 4))


def sign_ref(settings: Settings, kind: str, user_id: uuid.UUID, payload: dict[str, Any]) -> str:
    body = {
        "k": kind,
        "u": str(user_id),
        "exp": int(time.time()) + settings.signed_ref_ttl_minutes * 60,
        "d": payload,
    }
    raw = json.dumps(body, separators=(",", ":"), sort_keys=True).encode()
    sig = hmac.new(_key(settings, kind), raw, hashlib.sha256).digest()
    return f"{_b64(raw)}.{_b64(sig)}"


def verify_ref(settings: Settings, kind: str, user_id: uuid.UUID, token: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
    try:
        raw_b64, sig_b64 = token.split(".", 1)
        raw, sig = _unb64(raw_b64), _unb64(sig_b64)
        expected = hmac.new(_key(settings, kind), raw, hashlib.sha256).digest()
        if not hmac.compare_digest(sig, expected):
            raise InvalidRefError()
        body = json.loads(raw)
    except InvalidRefError:
        raise
    except (ValueError, TypeError):
        raise InvalidRefError() from None
    if (
        not isinstance(body, dict)
        or body.get("k") != kind
        or body.get("u") != str(user_id)  # a token is only valid for the user it was issued to
        or not isinstance(body.get("exp"), int)
        or body["exp"] < time.time()
        or not isinstance(body.get("d"), dict)
    ):
        raise InvalidRefError()
    return dict(body["d"])

from sqlalchemy import MetaData
from sqlalchemy.orm import DeclarativeBase

# Stable constraint names keep Alembic migrations deterministic across environments.
NAMING_CONVENTION = {
    "ix": "ix_%(column_0_label)s",
    "uq": "uq_%(table_name)s_%(column_0_name)s",
    "ck": "ck_%(table_name)s_%(constraint_name)s",
    "fk": "fk_%(table_name)s_%(column_0_name)s_%(referred_table_name)s",
    "pk": "pk_%(table_name)s",
}


class Base(DeclarativeBase):
    metadata = MetaData(naming_convention=NAMING_CONVENTION)

from collections.abc import Iterator
from functools import lru_cache

from sqlalchemy import Engine, create_engine
from sqlalchemy.orm import Session, sessionmaker

from app.core.config import get_settings


@lru_cache
def get_engine() -> Engine:
    return create_engine(get_settings().database_url, pool_pre_ping=True)


@lru_cache
def get_session_factory() -> sessionmaker[Session]:
    return sessionmaker(bind=get_engine(), expire_on_commit=False)


def get_db() -> Iterator[Session]:
    """FastAPI dependency: one session per request. Services commit explicitly."""
    session = get_session_factory()()
    try:
        yield session
    finally:
        session.close()

"""Deterministic allergen and diet rules.

This is the enforcement layer: a model cannot talk its way past it. Matching is on whole
normalised words so 'flour' does not match 'cauliflower'. The keyword tables are deliberately
conservative and small enough to review; they are not a regulatory allergen classification.
"""

import re
from dataclasses import dataclass

_WORD = re.compile(r"[a-z0-9']+")

# canonical allergen -> ingredient keywords that indicate it
ALLERGEN_KEYWORDS: dict[str, tuple[str, ...]] = {
    "peanut": ("peanut", "peanuts", "groundnut", "groundnuts"),
    "tree nut": (

        "pistachios", "hazelnut", "hazelnuts", "pecan", "pecans", "macadamia",
    ),
    "milk": (
        "milk", "butter", "buttermilk", "ghee", "cheese", "cream", "yoghurt", "yogurt",
        "paneer", "khoya", "kheer", "curd",
    ),
    "egg": ("egg", "eggs", "mayonnaise", "mayo", "omelette", "omelet"),
    "wheat": (
        "wheat", "flour", "maida", "atta", "bread", "breadcrumbs", "pasta", "spaghetti",
        "noodle", "noodles", "semolina", "sooji", "rava", "couscous", "malt",
    ),
    "soy": ("soy", "soya", "tofu", "tempeh", "edamame", "soybean", "soybeans"),
    "fish": ("fish", "salmon", "tuna", "cod", "tilapia", "anchovy", "anchovies", "sardine", "sardines", "mackerel"),
    "shellfish": (
        "shrimp", "prawn", "prawns", "crab", "lobster", "mussel", "mussels", "oyster",
        "oysters", "squid", "calamari", "clam", "clams", "scallop", "scallops",
    ),
    "sesame": ("sesame", "tahini", "til"),
    "mustard": ("mustard",),
}

MEAT = (
    "chicken", "beef", "pork", "lamb", "mutton", "goat", "bacon", "ham", "sausage",
    "salami", "pepperoni", "turkey", "duck", "venison", "meat", "mince", "steak",
)
SEAFOOD = ALLERGEN_KEYWORDS["fish"] + ALLERGEN_KEYWORDS["shellfish"]
ANIMAL_PRODUCT = ALLERGEN_KEYWORDS["milk"] + ALLERGEN_KEYWORDS["egg"] + ("honey", "gelatin")
ROOT_VEG = ("onion", "onions", "garlic", "potato", "potatoes", "carrot", "carrots", "radish", "beetroot", "beet")

DIET_FORBIDDEN: dict[str, tuple[str, ...]] = {
    "vegetarian": MEAT + SEAFOOD,
    "eggetarian": MEAT + SEAFOOD,
    "vegan": MEAT + SEAFOOD + ANIMAL_PRODUCT,
    "pescatarian": MEAT,
    "jain": MEAT + SEAFOOD + ROOT_VEG,
    "gluten_free": ALLERGEN_KEYWORDS["wheat"] + ("barley", "rye", "soy sauce"),
    "lactose_free": ALLERGEN_KEYWORDS["milk"],
}

# Diets a keyword table cannot verify. Recorded as an explicit caution, never silently accepted.
UNVERIFIABLE_DIETS: frozenset[str] = frozenset({"halal", "kosher"})

DIET_LABELS: dict[str, str] = {
    "vegetarian": "vegetarian",
    "eggetarian": "eggetarian",
    "vegan": "vegan",
    "pescatarian": "pescatarian",
    "jain": "Jain",
    "gluten_free": "gluten-free",
    "lactose_free": "lactose-free",
    "halal": "halal",
    "kosher": "kosher",
}


def _haystack(*texts: str) -> str:
    words = [w for text in texts for w in _WORD.findall(text.casefold())]
    return " " + " ".join(words) + " "


def _hits(hay: str, keywords: tuple[str, ...]) -> list[str]:
    return [k for k in keywords if f" {k} " in hay]


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Conflict:
    kind: str  # "allergy" | "diet"
    rule: str  # the user's allergen or diet
    ingredient: str  # the offending ingredient name (or the recipe title)
    matched: str  # the keyword that matched

    @property
    def message(self) -> str:
        label = f"your {self.rule} allergy" if self.kind == "allergy" else self.rule
        return f"“{self.ingredient}” contains “{self.matched}”, which conflicts with {label}."


def check_recipe(
    title: str, ingredient_names: list[str], allergies: list[str], diets: list[str]
) -> list[Conflict]:
    """Return every hard-constraint violation. Empty means the recipe is allowed."""
    conflicts: list[Conflict] = []
    for name in ingredient_names:
        hay = _haystack(name)
        for allergy in allergies:
            keywords = ALLERGEN_KEYWORDS.get(allergy.casefold())
            if keywords:
                for matched in _hits(hay, keywords):
                    conflicts.append(Conflict("allergy", allergy, name, matched))
        for diet in diets:
            keywords = DIET_FORBIDDEN.get(diet.casefold())
            if keywords:
                for matched in _hits(hay, keywords):
                    conflicts.append(Conflict("diet", diet, name, matched))
    # dedupe while preserving order
    seen: set[tuple[str, str, str, str]] = set()
    unique: list[Conflict] = []
    for c in conflicts:
        key = (c.kind, c.rule, c.ingredient, c.matched)
        if key not in seen:
            seen.add(key)
            unique.append(c)
    return unique


def declared_but_unverifiable(diets: list[str]) -> list[str]:
    return [d for d in diets if d.casefold() in UNVERIFIABLE_DIETS]


def allergens_present(ingredient_names: list[str]) -> list[str]:
    """Allergens detected from ingredient names (independent of the user's own declarations)."""
    found: list[str] = []
    hay = _haystack(*ingredient_names)
    for allergen, keywords in ALLERGEN_KEYWORDS.items():
        if _hits(hay, keywords):
            found.append(allergen)
    return found

"""Deterministic freshness/spoilage-sign assessment rules.

The vision model contributes **only evidence**: what it can see (colour changes, mould-like
growth, ...) and how usable the image is. Everything the user is told about it - the label, the
advice level, the reasons, the next steps and the food-specific cautions - is produced here, from
fixed rules and fixed text, so it can be reviewed, tested and cannot be "talked into" a
reassurance by a model or by text inside a photo.

Hard rules:
* There is no "safe" outcome. The best label is "no obvious visible concern in this image", and
  the guidance that accompanies it always says appearance cannot confirm safety.
* No percentage, score or probability of any kind.
* Missing, unclear or contradictory evidence yields "inconclusive", never a guess.
"""

import enum
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from datetime import date

    FISH_SEAFOOD = "fish_seafood"
    DAIRY_EGGS = "dairy_eggs"
    COOKED_FOOD = "cooked_food"
    BREAD_BAKED = "bread_baked"
    PACKAGED_SHELF_STABLE = "packaged_shelf_stable"
    OTHER = "other"


CATEGORY_LABELS: dict[FoodCategory, str] = {
    FoodCategory.FRUIT: "Fruit",
    FoodCategory.VEGETABLES: "Vegetables",
    FoodCategory.LEAFY_GREENS: "Leafy greens and herbs",
    FoodCategory.MEAT_POULTRY: "Meat and poultry",
    FoodCategory.FISH_SEAFOOD: "Fish and seafood",
    FoodCategory.DAIRY_EGGS: "Dairy and eggs",
    FoodCategory.COOKED_FOOD: "Cooked food and leftovers (including rice)",
    FoodCategory.BREAD_BAKED: "Bread and baked goods",
    FoodCategory.PACKAGED_SHELF_STABLE: "Packaged / tinned / shelf-stable food",

    "Do not eat it, and do not taste or sniff it to check.",
    "Throw it away in a sealed bag where children and pets cannot reach it.",

    "Mould can spread through soft or porous food where you cannot see it, so cutting away the "
    "visible patch is not a reliable fix."

    "Do not rely on how the food looks or smells. Check its date and how it was stored.",
    "If you cannot confirm it was stored safely and is within date, the safer choice is to "
    "discard it.",

_STEPS_GENERAL: tuple[str, ...] = (
    "No visible concern in a photo does not make the food safe. Check its date and storage "
    "history, and follow the guidance for this type of food below.",
    "If anything about its smell, texture, packaging or storage history seems off, discard it.",
)

_HOURS_ROOM_TEMP_LIMIT = 2
_COOKED_FRIDGE_LIMIT_HOURS = 4 * 24


def _label_for(evidence: ImageEvidence | None) -> tuple[VisualLabel, tuple[Reason, ...]]:
    def reasons(*codes: str) -> tuple[Reason, ...]:
        return tuple(Reason(c, INCONCLUSIVE_TEXT[c]) for c in codes)

    if evidence is None:
        return VisualLabel.INCONCLUSIVE, reasons("image_not_analysed")
    blocking: list[str] = []
    if not evidence.food_visible:
        blocking.append("no_food_visible")
    if evidence.image_quality is ImageQuality.UNUSABLE:
        blocking.append("image_unusable")
    if evidence.matches_confirmed_food == "no":
        blocking.append("food_mismatch")
    if blocking:
        return VisualLabel.INCONCLUSIVE, reasons(*blocking)
    if evidence.observations:
        return VisualLabel.VISIBLE_CONCERN, ()
    if evidence.image_quality is ImageQuality.CLEAR and evidence.matches_confirmed_food == "yes":
        return VisualLabel.NO_OBVIOUS_CONCERN, ()
    soft: list[str] = []
    if evidence.image_quality is not ImageQuality.CLEAR:
        soft.append("image_limited")
    if evidence.matches_confirmed_food == "unsure":
        soft.append("food_match_unsure")
    return VisualLabel.INCONCLUSIVE, reasons(*soft)


def assess(evidence: ImageEvidence | None, ctx: Context) -> Assessment:
    """Combine image evidence (may be None) with what the user told us. Pure and deterministic."""
    label, inconclusive = _label_for(evidence)
    high_risk = ctx.category in HIGH_RISK
    discard: list[Reason] = []
    caution: list[Reason] = []

    has_mold = bool(evidence) and any(
        o.feature is Feature.MOLD_LIKE_GROWTH for o in (evidence.observations if evidence else ())
    )
    if has_mold:
        discard.append(
            Reason(
                "mold_like_growth",
                "Mould-like growth was reported in the image (it may be certain or only "
                "possible). Mould can be accompanied by toxins and root deep into food.",
            )
        )
    if high_risk and label is VisualLabel.VISIBLE_CONCERN and not has_mold:
        discard.append(
            Reason(
                "visible_change_high_risk_food",
                "A visible change was reported on a food type where spoilage and harmful "
                "bacteria are a particular concern.",
            )
        )
    if (
        high_risk
        and ctx.storage is StorageCondition.ROOM_TEMPERATURE
        and ctx.storage_hours is not None
        and ctx.storage_hours > _HOURS_ROOM_TEMP_LIMIT
    ):
        discard.append(
            Reason(
                "left_out_too_long",
                "You said it was kept at room temperature for more than 2 hours. Perishable "
                "food left out that long should be discarded.",
            )
        )
    if (
        ctx.category is FoodCategory.COOKED_FOOD
        and ctx.storage is StorageCondition.REFRIGERATOR
        and ctx.storage_hours is not None
        and ctx.storage_hours > _COOKED_FRIDGE_LIMIT_HOURS
    ):
        discard.append(
            Reason(
                "leftovers_too_old",
                "Cooked leftovers kept in the fridge for more than about 4 days are beyond "
                "commonly published guidance.",
            )
        )
    if ctx.use_by is not None and ctx.use_by < ctx.assessed_on:
        entry = Reason(
            "use_by_passed",
            "The use-by date you entered has passed. Use-by dates relate to safety for "
            "perishable foods.",
        )
        (discard if high_risk else caution).append(entry)
    if ctx.best_before is not None and ctx.best_before < ctx.assessed_on:
        caution.append(
            Reason(
                "best_before_passed",
                "The best-before date you entered has passed. This is mainly a quality date, "
                "but check the food carefully and its storage history.",
            )
        )
    if label is VisualLabel.VISIBLE_CONCERN and not discard:
        caution.append(Reason("visible_concern", "A visible change was reported in the image."))
    if label is VisualLabel.INCONCLUSIVE:
        caution.append(
            Reason("inconclusive", "The image could not settle whether there is a visible concern.")
        )
    if high_risk and ctx.storage is StorageCondition.UNKNOWN:
        caution.append(
            Reason(
                "storage_unknown",
                "How this perishable food was stored is unknown, and storage matters more than "
                "appearance for this type of food.",
            )
        )

    if discard:
        level, reasons = AdviceLevel.DISCARD, tuple(discard + caution)
        steps = _STEPS_DISCARD + ((_STEP_MOLD,) if has_mold else ())
    elif caution:
        level, reasons = AdviceLevel.CAUTION, tuple(caution)
        steps = _STEPS_CAUTION
    else:
        level, reasons = AdviceLevel.GENERAL, ()
        steps = _STEPS_GENERAL

    return Assessment(
        label=label,
        inconclusive_reasons=inconclusive,
        advice_level=level,
        advice_reasons=reasons,
        steps=steps,
        category_cautions=CATEGORY_CAUTIONS[ctx.category],
        retake_tips=RETAKE_TIPS if label is VisualLabel.INCONCLUSIVE else (),
    )

"""Deterministic hygiene rules.

def highest_severity(severities: list[str]) -> str | None:
    present = [Severity(s) for s in severities if s in Severity._value2member_map_]
    if not present:
        return None
    return max(present, key=lambda s: SEVERITY_PRIORITY[s]).value

FILE: backend/app/domain/nutrition_calc.py

"""Deterministic nutrition arithmetic. No I/O, no AI, no estimation.

    nutrient amount = (nutrient per 100 g) x (grams eaten) / 100

Everything is computed with Decimal and rounded only once, at the output boundary (2 dp,
half-up). A total is the sum of the *unrounded* item amounts, so displayed item figures may differ
from the displayed total by a rounding hair, never more.

What this module refuses to do, by design:
  * infer a weight from a photo or a food name (a portion must be supplied by the user);
  * convert volume to weight (that needs a density nobody has verified);
  * treat a nutrient the source did not report as zero.

A portion given as a range yields a low and a high figure, and is flagged uncertain.
"""

from collections.abc import Mapping, Sequence
from dataclasses import dataclass
from decimal import ROUND_HALF_UP, Decimal

from app.nutrition.nutrients import NUTRIENTS

MASS_TO_GRAMS: dict[str, Decimal] = {
    "g": Decimal("1"),
    "kg": Decimal("1000"),
    "oz": Decimal("28.349523125"),  # international avoirdupois ounce
    "lb": Decimal("453.59237"),  # international avoirdupois pound
}
MIN_GRAMS = Decimal("0.1")
MAX_GRAMS = Decimal("5000")
_CENT = Decimal("0.01")


class PortionError(ValueError):
    """A portion that cannot be converted to grams safely. The message is user-facing."""


def to_decimal(value: float | int | str) -> Decimal:
    return Decimal(str(value))


def round_amount(value: Decimal) -> Decimal:
    return value.quantize(_CENT, rounding=ROUND_HALF_UP)


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Portion:
    grams_low: Decimal
    grams_high: Decimal
    uncertain: bool  # True when the user gave a range rather than a weight
    description: str


def _grams(amount: Decimal, unit: str) -> Decimal:
    factor = MASS_TO_GRAMS.get(unit)
    if factor is None:
        raise PortionError(
            f"'{unit}' cannot be converted to grams. Use g, kg, oz or lb. Volumes such as cups "
            "or millilitres depend on the food's density, so please enter a weight."
        )
    if amount <= 0:
        raise PortionError("A portion must be greater than zero.")
    grams = amount * factor
    if not MIN_GRAMS <= grams <= MAX_GRAMS:
        raise PortionError(
            f"A portion must be between {MIN_GRAMS} g and {MAX_GRAMS} g for a single food item."
        )
    return grams


def weight_portion(amount: float | str, unit: str) -> Portion:
    grams = _grams(to_decimal(amount), unit)
    return Portion(grams, grams, False, f"{to_decimal(amount).normalize():f} {unit}")


def range_portion(min_amount: float | str, max_amount: float | str, unit: str) -> Portion:
    low = _grams(to_decimal(min_amount), unit)
    high = _grams(to_decimal(max_amount), unit)
    if low >= high:
        raise PortionError("In a range, the minimum must be smaller than the maximum.")
    return Portion(
        low,
        high,
        True,
        f"{to_decimal(min_amount).normalize():f}-"
        f"{to_decimal(max_amount).normalize():f} {unit} (estimate)",
    )


def servings_portion(count: float | str, serving_grams: float | None) -> Portion:
    if serving_grams is None or serving_grams <= 0:
        raise PortionError(
            "This food's source does not give a serving size in grams. Please enter a weight."
        )
    grams = _grams(to_decimal(count) * to_decimal(serving_grams), "g")
    return Portion(
        grams,
        grams,
        False,
        f"{to_decimal(count).normalize():f} x {to_decimal(serving_grams).normalize():f} g serving",
    )


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class ItemInput:
    name: str
    per_100g: Mapping[str, float] | None  # None: no nutrition source was chosen for this item
    portion: Portion | None  # None: the user has not given a portion yet


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class ItemResult:
    name: str
    grams_low: Decimal | None
    grams_high: Decimal | None
    uncertain: bool
    has_nutrition_data: bool
    nutrients: dict[str, tuple[Decimal, Decimal]]  # key -> (low, high); only reported nutrients
    not_reported: tuple[str, ...]
    warnings: tuple[str, ...]


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class TotalNutrient:
    key: str
    low: Decimal | None  # None: no item reported this nutrient
    high: Decimal | None
    complete: bool  # True only if every item contributed
    contributing_items: int
    missing_items: tuple[str, ...]


def compute_item(item: ItemInput) -> ItemResult:
    warnings: list[str] = []
    if item.per_100g is None:
        warnings.append("no_nutrition_data")
    if item.portion is None:
        warnings.append("portion_missing")
    elif item.portion.uncertain:
        warnings.append("portion_is_estimate")

    nutrients: dict[str, tuple[Decimal, Decimal]] = {}
    not_reported: tuple[str, ...] = ()
    if item.per_100g is not None:
        not_reported = tuple(n.key for n in NUTRIENTS if n.key not in item.per_100g)
        if any(n.core and n.key not in item.per_100g for n in NUTRIENTS):
            warnings.append("partial_nutrients")
        if item.portion is not None:
            for n in NUTRIENTS:
                if n.key in item.per_100g:
                    per_100g = to_decimal(item.per_100g[n.key])
                    nutrients[n.key] = (
                        per_100g * item.portion.grams_low / 100,
                        per_100g * item.portion.grams_high / 100,
                    )
    return ItemResult(
        name=item.name,
        grams_low=item.portion.grams_low if item.portion else None,
        grams_high=item.portion.grams_high if item.portion else None,
        uncertain=bool(item.portion and item.portion.uncertain),
        has_nutrition_data=item.per_100g is not None,
        nutrients=nutrients,
        not_reported=not_reported,
        warnings=tuple(warnings),
    )


def compute_totals(results: Sequence[ItemResult]) -> dict[str, TotalNutrient]:
    totals: dict[str, TotalNutrient] = {}
    for n in NUTRIENTS:
        contributing = [r for r in results if n.key in r.nutrients]
        missing = tuple(r.name for r in results if n.key not in r.nutrients)
        low = (
            sum((r.nutrients[n.key][0] for r in contributing), Decimal(0)) if contributing else None
        )
        high = (
            sum((r.nutrients[n.key][1] for r in contributing), Decimal(0)) if contributing else None
        )
        totals[n.key] = TotalNutrient(
            key=n.key,
            low=low,
            high=high,
            complete=bool(results) and not missing,
            contributing_items=len(contributing),
            missing_items=missing,
        )
    return totals

FILE: backend/app/domain/recipes.py

"""Deterministic recipe arithmetic and structural checks. No AI, no I/O."""

from decimal import ROUND_HALF_UP, Decimal

from app.ai.cooking import IngredientIn, RecipeDraft
from app.domain.diet_rules import Conflict, allergens_present, check_recipe
from app.schemas.food import TotalOut

MAX_SERVINGS = 24
_CENT = Decimal("0.01")


class RecipeError(ValueError):
    """A recipe that cannot be used. The message is user-facing."""


def _round(value: Decimal) -> float:
    return float(value.quantize(_CENT, rounding=ROUND_HALF_UP))


def scale_ingredient(ingredient: IngredientIn, factor: Decimal) -> IngredientIn:
    if ingredient.quantity is None:
        return ingredient
    scaled = Decimal(str(ingredient.quantity)) * factor
    return ingredient.model_copy(update={"quantity": _round(scaled)})


def scale_recipe(recipe: RecipeDraft, servings: int) -> RecipeDraft:
    """Scale to a new serving count. Numeric quantities scale; free-text stays as written."""
    if not 1 <= servings <= MAX_SERVINGS:
        raise RecipeError(f"A recipe can serve between 1 and {MAX_SERVINGS} people.")
    if servings == recipe.servings:
        return recipe
    factor = Decimal(servings) / Decimal(recipe.servings)
    return recipe.model_copy(
        update={
            "servings": servings,
            "ingredients": [scale_ingredient(i, factor) for i in recipe.ingredients],
        }
    )


def enforce(
    recipe: RecipeDraft, allergies: list[str], diets: list[str]
) -> list[Conflict]:
    """The hard gate. A non-empty result means the recipe must not be stored or shown."""
    names = [i.name for i in recipe.ingredients]
    if not names:
        raise RecipeError("A recipe must have at least one ingredient.")
    return check_recipe(recipe.title, names, allergies, diets)


def allergy_disclosure(recipe: RecipeDraft, allergies: list[str]) -> dict[str, list[str]]:
    """What the app asserts independently of the model."""
    detected = allergens_present([i.name for i in recipe.ingredients])
    warnings = [
        "This ingredient list is a suggestion, not a label. Check every package and ask about "
        "cross-contact wherever the food was prepared or bought.",
    ]
    if detected:
        warnings.append("Allergens detected in the ingredients: " + ", ".join(detected) + ".")
    if allergies:
        warnings.append(
            "Your declared allergies were checked against the ingredient names: "
            + ", ".join(allergies)
            + "."
        )
    return {"detected_allergens": detected, "warnings": warnings}


def divide_totals(totals: dict[str, TotalOut], servings: int) -> dict[str, TotalOut]:
    """Per-serving figures from whole-recipe totals (deterministic, half-up to 2 dp)."""
    if servings < 1:
        raise RecipeError("Servings must be at least 1.")
    divisor = Decimal(servings)
    out: dict[str, TotalOut] = {}
    for key, total in totals.items():
        low = total.low if total.low is not None else None
        high = total.high if total.high is not None else None
        out[key] = total.model_copy(
            update={
                "low": _round(Decimal(str(low)) / divisor) if low is not None else None,
                "high": _round(Decimal(str(high)) / divisor) if high is not None else None,
            }
        )
    return out

================================================================================
FILE: backend/app/media/storage.py
================================================================================

"""Storage abstraction for media bytes.

Services depend only on the StorageBackend protocol. LocalStorage is the development
implementation; an S3-compatible backend can implement the same four methods later without
touching services or routes. Keys are always server-generated; LocalStorage still re-validates
every key so a bug elsewhere can never turn into path traversal.
"""

import contextlib
import os
import re
import tempfile
from collections.abc import Iterator
from pathlib import Path
from typing import BinaryIO, Protocol

_KEY_RE = re.compile(r"^[0-9a-f]{2}/[0-9a-f]{32}\.(jpg|png|webp)$")
_CHUNK = 64 * 1024


class StorageError(Exception):
    pass


class StorageBackend(Protocol):
    def put(self, key: str, data: bytes) -> None: ...
    def open(self, key: str) -> BinaryIO: ...
    def delete(self, key: str) -> None: ...
    def exists(self, key: str) -> bool: ...


class LocalStorage:
    def __init__(self, root: Path) -> None:
        self._root = root.resolve()

    def _path(self, key: str) -> Path:
        if not _KEY_RE.fullmatch(key):
            raise StorageError("invalid storage key")
        path = (self._root / key).resolve()
        if not path.is_relative_to(self._root):
            raise StorageError("invalid storage key")
        return path

    def put(self, key: str, data: bytes) -> None:
        path = self._path(key)
        path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True, mode=0o700)
        # Write to a temp file in the same directory, then rename: readers never see a
        # partial file and a crash never leaves a truncated one under the final name.
        fd, tmp = tempfile.mkstemp(dir=path.parent, prefix=".tmp-")
        try:
            with os.fdopen(fd, "wb") as fh:
                fh.write(data)
            os.chmod(tmp, 0o600)
            os.replace(tmp, path)
        except BaseException:
            with contextlib.suppress(OSError):
                os.unlink(tmp)
            raise

    def open(self, key: str) -> BinaryIO:
        try:
            return self._path(key).open("rb")
        except FileNotFoundError as exc:
            raise StorageError("object not found") from exc

    def delete(self, key: str) -> None:
        with contextlib.suppress(FileNotFoundError):
            self._path(key).unlink()

    def exists(self, key: str) -> bool:
        return self._path(key).is_file()


def iter_chunks(fh: BinaryIO) -> Iterator[bytes]:
    try:
        while chunk := fh.read(_CHUNK):
            yield chunk
    finally:
        fh.close()

FILE: backend/app/media/validation.py
================================================================================

"""Upload validation and image re-encoding.

Nothing the client says is trusted: not the filename, not the Content-Type header, not the
extension. The bytes are inspected (signature), then fully decoded and re-encoded by Pillow,
which drops EXIF/GPS and any trailing or polyglot payload. The stored file is the re-encoded
output, never the original upload.

Only images are enabled. Video and audio need their own signature checks, decoders and a
duration probe (Phase 7); until then they are rejected explicitly rather than half-validated.
"""

import io
import re
import unicodedata
import warnings
from dataclasses import dataclass

from PIL import Image, ImageOps, UnidentifiedImageError

from app.core.errors import AppError, UnsupportedMediaTypeError
from app.models.media import MediaKind


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class ImageFormat:
    pil_format: str
    content_type: str
    extension: str  # canonical, used in the storage key
    accepted_extensions: frozenset[str]


IMAGE_FORMATS: dict[str, ImageFormat] = {
    "jpeg": ImageFormat("JPEG", "image/jpeg", "jpg", frozenset({".jpg", ".jpeg"})),
    "png": ImageFormat("PNG", "image/png", "png", frozenset({".png"})),
    "webp": ImageFormat("WEBP", "image/webp", "webp", frozenset({".webp"})),
}

# Recognised only so we can say "not enabled yet" instead of "unknown"; never accepted.
_RESERVED_EXTENSIONS = frozenset(
    {".mp4", ".mov", ".webm", ".mkv", ".avi", ".mp3", ".wav", ".m4a", ".ogg", ".aac", ".flac"}
)


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class ProcessedMedia:
    kind: MediaKind
    content_type: str
    extension: str
    data: bytes
    width: int
    height: int
    duration_seconds: float | None = None


def _invalid(message: str, code: str = "invalid_image") -> AppError:
    return AppError(message, code=code, status_code=422)


def sniff_image(head: bytes) -> str | None:
    """Identify an image by its signature. Returns a key of IMAGE_FORMATS or None."""
    if head.startswith(b"\xff\xd8\xff"):
        return "jpeg"
    if head.startswith(b"\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n"):
        return "png"
    if len(head) >= 12 and head[:4] == b"RIFF" and head[8:12] == b"WEBP":
        return "webp"
    return None


_UNSAFE_NAME_CHARS = re.compile(r'[\x00-\x1f\x7f<>:"|?*\\/]')


def sanitize_display_name(name: str | None) -> str:
    """A safe label for the UI. It is never used for storage paths."""
    if not name:
        return "image"
    name = name.replace("\\", "/").rsplit("/", 1)[-1]
    name = unicodedata.normalize("NFC", name)
    name = _UNSAFE_NAME_CHARS.sub("", name)
    name = " ".join(name.split()).strip(" .")
    return name[:120] or "image"


def _extension(filename: str | None) -> str:
    if not filename or "." not in filename:
        return ""
    return "." + filename.replace("\\", "/").rsplit("/", 1)[-1].rsplit(".", 1)[-1].lower()


def _normalise_mime(value: str | None) -> str:
    return (value or "").split(";", 1)[0].strip().lower()


def validate_and_process(
    data: bytes, filename: str | None, declared_content_type: str | None, max_pixels: int
) -> ProcessedMedia:
    if not data:
        raise _invalid("The uploaded file is empty.", "empty_file")

    ext = _extension(filename)
    if ext in _RESERVED_EXTENSIONS:
        raise UnsupportedMediaTypeError(
            "Video and audio uploads are not enabled yet. Upload a JPEG, PNG or WebP image.",
            code="media_kind_not_enabled",
        )

    detected = sniff_image(data[:16])
    if detected is None:
        raise UnsupportedMediaTypeError("Only JPEG, PNG and WebP images are supported.")
    fmt = IMAGE_FORMATS[detected]

    # The extension and declared type must agree with what the bytes really are.
    if (
        ext not in fmt.accepted_extensions
        or _normalise_mime(declared_content_type) != fmt.content_type
    ):
        raise UnsupportedMediaTypeError(
            "The file name or declared type does not match the file contents.",
            code="media_type_mismatch",
        )

    try:
        with warnings.catch_warnings():
            warnings.simplefilter("error", Image.DecompressionBombWarning)
            with Image.open(io.BytesIO(data)) as probe:
                if probe.format != fmt.pil_format:
                    raise _invalid("The file is not a valid image.")
                width, height = probe.size
                if width < 1 or height < 1 or width * height > max_pixels:
                    raise _invalid(
                        "The image dimensions are too large.", code="image_dimensions_too_large"
                    )
                probe.load()  # fully decode now; truncated/corrupt files raise here
                image = ImageOps.exif_transpose(
                    probe
                )  # bake in orientation before metadata is dropped
                out = _encode(image, fmt)
                width, height = image.size
    except AppError:
        raise
    except (
        UnidentifiedImageError,
        Image.DecompressionBombError,
        Image.DecompressionBombWarning,
        OSError,
        ValueError,
        SyntaxError,
    ):
        raise _invalid("The file could not be decoded as a valid image.") from None

    return ProcessedMedia(
        kind=MediaKind.IMAGE,
        content_type=fmt.content_type,
        extension=fmt.extension,
        data=out,
        width=width,
        height=height,
    )


def _encode(image: Image.Image, fmt: ImageFormat) -> bytes:
    buf = io.BytesIO()
    if fmt.pil_format == "JPEG":
        if image.mode not in ("RGB", "L"):
            image = image.convert("RGB")
        image.save(buf, "JPEG", quality=90, optimize=True)  # no exif= argument: metadata dropped
    elif fmt.pil_format == "PNG":
        image.save(buf, "PNG", optimize=True)
    else:
        if image.mode not in ("RGB", "RGBA"):
            has_alpha = "A" in image.mode or "transparency" in image.info
            image = image.convert("RGBA" if has_alpha else "RGB")
        image.save(buf, "WEBP", quality=90)
    return buf.getvalue()

import enum
import uuid
from datetime import datetime
from typing import Any

from sqlalchemy import DateTime, Enum, ForeignKey, Index, String, Text, func
from sqlalchemy.dialects.postgresql import JSONB, UUID
from sqlalchemy.orm import Mapped, mapped_column

from app.db.base import Base


class ModuleKey(enum.StrEnum):
    FOOD_RECOGNITION = "food_recognition"
    FRESHNESS = "freshness"
    HYGIENE = "hygiene"
    COOKING = "cooking"
    MEAL_PLANNING = "meal_planning"


class AnalysisStatus(enum.StrEnum):
    PENDING = "pending"
    COMPLETED = "completed"
    FAILED = "failed"


def _enum(e: type[enum.StrEnum], name: str) -> Enum:
    return Enum(
        e,
        name=name,
        native_enum=False,
        create_constraint=True,
        values_callable=lambda x: [m.value for m in x],
        length=32,
    )


class AnalysisRecord(Base):
    """One entry in a user's activity history, shared by every feature module.

    Phase 2 creates the table and read/delete access only. Feature modules (later phases)
    are the only writers; nothing in this phase inserts records.
    """

    __tablename__ = "analysis_records"
    __table_args__ = (Index("ix_analysis_records_owner_created", "owner_id", "created_at"),)

    id: Mapped[uuid.UUID] = mapped_column(UUID(as_uuid=True), primary_key=True, default=uuid.uuid4)
    owner_id: Mapped[uuid.UUID] = mapped_column(
        UUID(as_uuid=True), ForeignKey("users.id", ondelete="CASCADE")
    )
    module: Mapped[ModuleKey] = mapped_column(_enum(ModuleKey, "module_key"))
    status: Mapped[AnalysisStatus] = mapped_column(_enum(AnalysisStatus, "analysis_status"))
    title: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(String(200))
    summary: Mapped[str | None] = mapped_column(Text, nullable=True)
    # Structured, module-specific output. Shape is defined by each module's own schema.
    result: Mapped[dict[str, Any] | None] = mapped_column(JSONB, nullable=True)
    media_id: Mapped[uuid.UUID | None] = mapped_column(
        UUID(as_uuid=True), ForeignKey("media_assets.id", ondelete="SET NULL"), nullable=True
    )
    created_at: Mapped[datetime] = mapped_column(DateTime(timezone=True), server_default=func.now())

    SAVED = "saved"

    USER = "user"
    ASSISTANT = "assistant"

class Recipe(Base):
    """A model-suggested recipe. `id` equals the AnalysisRecord id once saved, so a recipe
    and its history entry share one identity and deleting either removes both."""

    __tablename__ = "recipes"
    __table_args__ = (
        Index("ix_recipes_owner_created", "owner_id", "created_at"),
        Index("ix_recipes_owner_title", "owner_id", "title"),
    )

    id: Mapped[uuid.UUID] = mapped_column(
        UUID(as_uuid=True), primary_key=True, default=uuid.uuid4
    )
    analysis_id: Mapped[uuid.UUID | None] = mapped_column(
        UUID(as_uuid=True),
        ForeignKey("analysis_records.id", ondelete="CASCADE"),
        unique=True,
        nullable=True,
    )
    owner_id: Mapped[uuid.UUID] = mapped_column(
        UUID(as_uuid=True), ForeignKey("users.id", ondelete="CASCADE")

================================================================================
FILE: backend/app/nutrition/import_reference.py
================================================================================

"""Import an offline reference table (such as IFCT) from a CSV file you supply.

    python -m app.nutrition.import_reference foods.csv --dataset "IFCT 2017" --version 2017 \\
        --citation "Longvah T. et al., Indian Food Composition Tables 2017, ICMR-NIN" \\
        --license-note "Used under the dataset's terms; verify before redistribution."

CSV header: source_id,name[,category] followed by any of the nutrient columns
(energy_kcal, protein_g, carbs_g, fat_g, fiber_g, sugars_g, saturated_fat_g, sodium_mg), all per
100 g. An empty cell means "the dataset does not report this" and is stored as absent, never 0.
Rows are upserted by (dataset, source_id); nothing is ever deleted. Dataset, version, citation and
licence note are mandatory so every stored value stays traceable.
"""

import argparse
import csv
import sys
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from pathlib import Path

from sqlalchemy import select
from sqlalchemy.orm import Session

from app.models.reference import ReferenceFood
from app.nutrition.nutrients import NUTRIENT_BY_KEY
from app.nutrition.sources.local import normalise


@dataclass
class ImportResult:
    inserted: int = 0
    updated: int = 0
    errors: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)


def import_csv(
    db: Session, path: Path, *, dataset: str, version: str, citation: str, license_note: str
) -> ImportResult:
    for label, value in (
        ("dataset", dataset),
        ("version", version),
        ("citation", citation),
        ("license note", license_note),
    ):
        if not value.strip():
            raise ValueError(f"A non-empty {label} is required so every value stays traceable.")

    result = ImportResult()
    with path.open(newline="", encoding="utf-8-sig") as fh:
        reader = csv.DictReader(fh)
        columns = set(reader.fieldnames or [])
        allowed = {"source_id", "name", "category", *NUTRIENT_BY_KEY}
        unknown = columns - allowed
        if unknown:
            raise ValueError(f"Unknown columns: {sorted(unknown)}")
        if not {"source_id", "name"} <= columns:
            raise ValueError("The CSV needs 'source_id' and 'name' columns.")

        for line, row in enumerate(reader, start=2):
            source_id = (row.get("source_id") or "").strip()
            name = (row.get("name") or "").strip()
            if not source_id or not name:
                result.errors.append(f"line {line}: source_id and name are required")
                continue
            nutrients: dict[str, float] = {}
            bad = False
            for key in NUTRIENT_BY_KEY:
                raw = (row.get(key) or "").strip()
                if raw == "":
                    continue
                try:
                    number = float(raw)
                except ValueError:
                    result.errors.append(f"line {line}: {key} is not a number")
                    bad = True
                    break
                if not 0 <= number <= NUTRIENT_BY_KEY[key].max_per_100g:
                    result.errors.append(f"line {line}: {key} is out of range")
                    bad = True
                    break
                nutrients[key] = number
            if bad:
                continue
            if not nutrients:
                result.errors.append(f"line {line}: no nutrient values")
                continue

            existing = db.scalar(
                select(ReferenceFood).where(
                    ReferenceFood.dataset == dataset, ReferenceFood.source_id == source_id
                )
            )
            category = (row.get("category") or "").strip() or None
            if existing is None:
                db.add(
                    ReferenceFood(
                        dataset=dataset,
                        dataset_version=version,
                        source_id=source_id,
                        name=name[:200],
                        name_normalized=normalise(name)[:200],
                        category=category,
                        nutrients=nutrients,
                        citation=citation,
                        license_note=license_note,
                    )
                )
                result.inserted += 1
            else:
                existing.dataset_version = version
                existing.name = name[:200]
                existing.name_normalized = normalise(name)[:200]
                existing.category = category
                existing.nutrients = nutrients
                existing.citation = citation
                existing.license_note = license_note
                result.updated += 1
    db.commit()
    return result


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(
        description=__doc__, formatter_class=argparse.RawTextHelpFormatter
    )
    parser.add_argument("csv_file", type=Path)
    parser.add_argument("--dataset", required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--version", required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--citation", required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--license-note", required=True)
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)

    from app.db.session import get_session_factory

    with get_session_factory()() as db:
        try:
            result = import_csv(
                db,
                args.csv_file,
                dataset=args.dataset,
                version=args.version,
                citation=args.citation,
                license_note=args.license_note,
            )
        except (ValueError, OSError) as exc:
            print(f"Import failed: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)
            return 1
    print(f"Inserted {result.inserted}, updated {result.updated}, skipped {len(result.errors)}.")
    for err in result.errors[:20]:
        print(f"  - {err}", file=sys.stderr)
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

FILE: backend/app/nutrition/nutrients.py
